<!-- docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Every entry below is a failure mode hit while building this project,
with the fix that resolved it. Symptoms first.

## Everyone bounces to sign-in (including fresh logins)

The middleware's cookie names don't match the engine's. The names in
`lib/auth-cookie-names.ts` must mirror the engine options exactly —
custom `advanced.cookies` names (Better Auth) or
`cookies.sessionToken.name` (Auth.js) included. A mismatch fails closed by design. Compare the
`set-cookie` response headers against your names list.

## Auth.js sign-in shows the form error, or lands on the Auth.js error page

The credentials callback always 302s; read the final URL (see the
[Auth.js guide](guide-authjs.md)). If _every_ login fails, check the
server log for `CredentialsSignin` (wrong password / unknown user —
expected for bad credentials) versus `Configuration` (missing
secret, untrusted host). If the user exists but login never sticks,
the row is unverified — the plugin links verified identities only.

## `UnsupportedStrategy` 500s on every Auth.js action

Credentials + database session strategy. Auth.js rejects that
combination at config time; the engine fail-fasts first — including
through factory-wrapped providers, which it inspects by calling them
with `{}` exactly as Auth.js does
(`packages/provider-authjs/src/engine.ts`, covered by the engine
suite's factory tests). A credentials provider in any form without
explicit `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }` throws at wiring with the fix
attached; a factory that throws on inspection fails at wiring as
`provider factory threw` (Auth.js would throw identically on first
request — the factory must tolerate `{}`).

So a request-time 500 means a genuine problem, not an inspection
miss: either the served config really lacks the jwt strategy (check
that the route serves the engine's `config` — a hand-composed `Auth()`
bypasses the fail-fast), or a factory threw (read the wiring error,
not the 500 page). Fix: `Credentials(...)` — direct or via a
`{}`-tolerant factory — with explicit `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }`.

## `AdapterMappingError` / `UnsupportedSchemaError` on login

A storage row is corrupt (missing id field, wrong date shape, account
without `userId`). Auth.js throws `AdapterMappingError` naming the
field — inspect the `aj-*` row directly. Better Auth's equivalent
fail-fast is `UnsupportedSchemaError` on the `ba-*` row. Fix or
delete the row; this never becomes a silent login failure — that is
the point.

The same error at **boot** (not login) usually means a Better Auth
plugin contributes a field or model this adapter has not declared.
Two satellite packages are known-unprobed today — `@better-auth/api-key`
and `@better-auth/sso`: composing them fails fast with
`UnsupportedSchemaError` until support lands; every plugin exported
by `better-auth/plugins` plus `@better-auth/passkey` is covered by
the committed schema probe.

## `SQLITE_ERROR: no such column: …` (or `42703` on Postgres) at boot or on first use

The code is newer than the database: a column this version selects
or writes does not exist in your tables. This is the raw shape of an
**unmigrated upgrade** (B1) — the 0.1.1 → 0.2.0 move added
`aj-verification-tokens.key` and the `users` governance fields, and
booting 0.2.x on an unmigrated 0.1.1 database died exactly this way
on the first `users` query.

Map the missing column to the fix:

- `users.phone` / `users.suspendedUntil` / `users.suspendReason` →
  0.1.1 → 0.2.x upgrade steps in
  [upgrading.md](upgrading.md#011--020): boot once with push on
  (dev), or generate/apply the migration (production). All three
  columns are optional; no backfill needed.
- `aj_verification_tokens.key` → same section. After a 0.2.1+ boot
  the column exists nullable; if your database instead shows the
  old table recreation damage (empty `aj-verification-tokens`,
  half-migrated `ba_users` on SQLite), that was 0.2.0-exact with
  push on — restore from backup or re-create the token rows, then
  upgrade to 0.2.1+.
- On MongoDB you will never see this error — drift surfaces as
  silently wrong indexes instead. If you upgraded the Auth.js
  provider and the composite-token behavior seems absent, run
  `reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes(payload)` (see the 0.1.1 → 0.2.0
  section).
- Column exists but a `NOT NULL` insert fails (`key`) → an old
  0.2.0 migration made it required; drop and re-add it nullable per
  the upgrading.md SQL sketch.

Prevention: upgrade through one version heading at a time, keep
`bun run schema:check`-style migration review in your deploy, and
check `docs/upgrading.md` for the version you are adopting before
bumping. The runtime `UnsupportedVersionError` catches upstream
version drift at boot; missing columns mean the **database** half
of an upgrade was skipped.

## `UnsupportedVersionError` at boot

An upstream (`payload`, `better-auth`, `@auth/core`) sits outside
the validated band — found vs supported are both in the message.
Pin the named package back inside the band (exact versions in
[compatibility.md](compatibility.md)) and wait for the compat patch
that widens it. The refusal happens before any database write by
design: an unvalidated upstream must not touch your data.

## Edge build fails importing `payload` / database code

Something in `middleware.ts`'s import graph reaches the engine or
`payload.config`. Middleware must import _only_ the cookie-names
module (which uses the `/cookies` subpaths). The classic trap: a
shared `lib/auth.ts` exporting both the engine and the names —
split them, as the example does.

## Session endpoint 401s with a live provider session

- **Unverified email.** Provider session exists, plugin linking
  refused. Verify the user (Better Auth: complete verification;
  Auth.js credentials: stamp `emailVerified`).
- **Missing origin (Auth.js / verifier).** Without `baseURL`
  (`AUTH_URL`) the internal session request falls back to the live
  `host`/`x-forwarded-host` headers. Proxies that strip host break
  it — and spoofed host headers would redirect the forwarded
  session cookie, so set the canonical origin in production
  instead of relying on the fallback.
- **Clock skew.** Expiry checks run against the injected clock;
  wild skew reads as expired.

## Changes don't take effect locally

Stale `dist` — cross-package workspace imports resolve `dist`, not
`src` (same-package unit tests import `src` relatively and are
unaffected). `bun run build` after cross-package core changes. (The
`e2e` and `dev:example` scripts build first; ad-hoc `next dev` does
not.)

## Postgres parity run fails to boot

`bun run e2e:postgres` expects Postgres at `localhost:5433`
(`postgres` / `payload`): `docker run -d --name pal-pg -e
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=payload -p 5433:5432 postgres:16`. Override with
`PGHOST` / `PGPORT` / `PGUSER` / `PGPASSWORD` / `DATABASE_URL`.

## Mongo parity run throws lock/write conflicts

Single-node memory-server transients under concurrent transactions.
The example's mongo branch already disables transactions and uses
wiredTiger — if you re-enable transactions, expect `LockTimeout` /
`WriteConflict` flakes. Never "fix" these with product-code retries;
they are a test-environment artifact (real replica sets don't
behave this way).

## `attw` / `publint` failures on release

Run `bun run release:check`. `attw` must use `--profile esm-only`
(all packages are ESM-only by decision — legacy node10/CJS
resolution failures are the documented tradeoff). If `publint`
complains about missing files, check the package `files` list and
the `exports` map agree.

---

<!-- docs/upgrading.md -->

# Upgrading

Versioning rides [changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets):
every user-facing change ships a changeset, the release workflow
opens Version Packages PRs, and each package CHANGELOG records what
moved. This page covers the moves that need human attention —
especially database moves, where an unattended upgrade has historically
meant an unbootable app (see the per-adapter steps under each version
heading before you bump).

## Pre-1.0 policy

Minor versions may break: the wire contract (`SessionUser`, endpoint
paths, cookie semantics) is the stability anchor and changes only
with a migration note here; option shapes and internal ports may
evolve. Read the package CHANGELOGs on every bump.

## Supported bands and the version assertion

The validated bands live in [compatibility.md](compatibility.md) and
equal the CI compat matrix ({floor, latest} per upstream). At wiring
time every package asserts the upstream versions it drives:

- the plugin checks `payload` (`supportedPayloadBand`),
- `provider-better-auth` checks `better-auth` (`supportedBetterAuthBand`),
- `provider-authjs` checks `@auth/core` (`supportedAuthJsBand`).

An out-of-band version throws `UnsupportedVersionError` (found vs
supported + a pointer here) **before any collection write** — an
unsupported upstream fails at startup with a typed, actionable error,
never as a raw SQL error or a missing-adapter `TypeError`
mid-request. When it fires: pin the upstream back inside the band
and wait for (or cut) a compat patch that widens the band after the
matrix proves the new version. Prerelease builds only ever match via
an explicit `exact` entry — canaries never float in through a range.

## 0.1.1 → 0.2.0

What changed in the database (and nothing else did — provider
collection shapes otherwise moved zero columns):

- **`users`** gains three optional governance fields: `phone`
  (text), `suspendedUntil` (date), `suspendReason` (text). All
  nullable and additive — safe on every adapter, every mode.
- **`aj-verification-tokens`** (Auth.js provider): `token` loses its
  standalone unique index; a new nullable unique `key` column
  identifies a token by its `(identifier, token-hash)` pair. This is
  the composite-key fix: the same OTP hash may now exist for two
  different identifiers. The `key` column is **nullable** — pre-fix
  releases shipped it `required`, which is what made upgraded
  databases unbootable (see below); 0.2.1+ accepts `NULL` keys and
  backfills lazily on write.
- **`ba-*` collections** (Better Auth provider): no shape change.

Verification tokens are **not** invalidated: existing rows keep
working (the adapter reads by `(identifier, token)` and tolerates
`NULL` keys). No data loss on any adapter.

**SQLite, dev-push (Payload `push: true`):** just boot the new
version. Adding a nullable column alters the table in place — no
data-loss prompt, no table rebuild. (0.2.0 exactly shipped `key` as
required; booting it hangs on drizzle's data-loss prompt and can
recreate the token table empty. Upgrade straight to 0.2.1+.)

**Postgres, dev-push:** same — the column adds in place and the
unique index swaps `token` → `key`. (0.2.0 exactly hung on the same
prompt; Postgres converged if you accepted, but the token table
emptied.)

**Production (migrations mode):** generate the migration yourself
(`payload.migrate:create`) and check it adds `key` as a **nullable**
column and drops the `token` unique index — `ADD COLUMN key TEXT`
without `NOT NULL`. On a non-empty table, a NOT NULL variant fails
outright (`column "key" contains null values`); a nullable one is a
no-loss step. See the [migrations recipe](#running-production-on-migrations-not-push).

**MongoDB:** schema drift cannot crash Mongo, but index lifecycle is
the trap: Payload's adapter never drops indexes, so the **stale
`token` unique index survives the upgrade** (silently keeping the
pre-0.2.0 "one row per token hash" constraint), and the added `key`
unique index builds in the background over rows without the field.
Fix with the idempotent reconciliation helper:

```ts
import { reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes } from '@payload-auth-link/provider-authjs'

const report = await reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes(payload)
// { status: 'reconciled', droppedStaleTokenIndex, backfilledKeys, keyIndex }
```

It backfills `key` (`JSON.stringify([identifier, tokenHash])`),
drops the stale `token` unique index, and reports (rather than
throws) when the `key` index build is still in flight. Run it once
per deployment after upgrading (idempotent; safe to re-run).
Already upgraded without it? The composite-key behavior silently
does not hold on your deployment until you run the reconciliation.

## 0.3.x → 0.3.1 (security default change)

The injected users-collection fields now fail closed
(GHSA-2m5q-cqr7-45xc). Previously, Payload's own defaults made every
authenticated user able to write every field of every user document —
including `roles`. The new default policy:

- **Writes** to `roles`, `phone`, `suspendedUntil`, `suspendReason`
  require the **role-manager roles** — the new `roleManagerRoles`
  option, defaulting to `['admin']`. If your configured `roles` have
  no `admin`, the plugin refuses to boot without an explicit
  `roleManagerRoles: [...]`. Editors holding a non-admin role must be
  named there or they lose the ability to edit roles in the admin
  panel.
- **Reads** of `suspendReason`, `suspendedUntil` and `identities` are
  role-manager only; `identities` writes are denied to REST and the
  admin panel entirely (the engine manages linking through the Local
  API, which is unaffected).
- The **admin panel** is no longer granted to "any signed-in user":
  the default grant is the role-manager roles. Declare
  `access: { admin: ... }` on your users collection to restore a
  wider policy — the plugin wraps your function with the
  impersonation deny and otherwise leaves it alone.
- Local-API writes (`overrideAccess`) — the plugin's engine paths and
  your own scripts — are never restricted by any of this.

If you depended on users editing their own profile fields, declare
those fields' access explicitly; the plugin never guesses a policy
for fields it did not inject. The negative behaviour is pinned by
`e2e/access.spec.ts` (non-admin escalation, admin-panel entry, field
stripping, manager writes) across all six adapter/example combos.

## 0.2.x → 0.3.0

Install-level changes — read before bumping:

- **`better-auth` and `@auth/core` moved from dependencies to
  peers.** The providers no longer install them for you. If you
  already import them (you almost certainly do — you configure the
  BA server or the Auth.js providers), add them explicitly:

  ```sh
  # Better Auth tree
  bun add better-auth@1.7          # validated band: >=1.7.6 <1.8.0
  # Auth.js tree
  bun add @auth/core@0.41          # validated band: >=0.41.0 <0.42.0
  ```

  Missing peers fail at install time with a clear "unmet peer" (npm)
  or auto-install-warn (bun) — not with a runtime module-not-found
  three frames deep. The narrow bands are the point: a fresh install
  can no longer resolve an upstream minor nobody validated. Widening
  is a compat patch away once the matrix proves the new version.

- **`payload` peers tightened to `^3.83.0 || 4.0.0-beta.0`.** 3.83.0
  is the bisected floor for the named-plugin and global-hook APIs the
  plugin uses; the v4 pin is the exact tested beta (no caret — v4
  canaries were silently inside the old range and broken).
- **Framework peers got honest floors:** `next` is now
  `^15.0.0 || ^16.0.0` (16 e2e-tested by the examples), and
  TanStack Start is `^1.140.2` (the first version with the
  `createMiddleware` types the adapter uses) with
  `@tanstack/react-router` `^1.170.0`.
- **Runtime version assertions** are live (see above). On a peer
  outside the band you get `UnsupportedVersionError` at boot —
  actionable, before any write.
- **Role-config safety:** removing a role from
  `authLink({ roles })` now stops granting it on the next session
  (stored values are filtered at read time), and the first boot
  after the change logs one aggregate warning naming the drifted
  values and affected user count. See the
  [role runbook](#changing-or-removing-roles) before trimming roles.

No database shape changes in this line: the collection snapshots are
byte-identical to 0.2.x (enforced by `bun run schema:check` from
here on — a PR that changes a shape must carry an `Upgrade impact:`
changeset section and an entry in this file, or CI fails).

## Rolling deploys and rollback (N and N−1)

The compatibility criterion, tested by the golden-DB suite on every
change: **the previous minor boots and serves core flows on the new
schema, and the new minor serves pre-migration rows.** Concretely,
during a rolling deploy or a rollback:

- 0.1.1 code on a 0.2.x database works — extra nullable columns are
  ignored, and old Auth.js token writes (`key` absent) are accepted
  by the nullable unique index. Rollback is data-safe.
- Caveat: an old pod cannot know fields it predates (e.g.
  `suspendedUntil`), so a suspended user keeps verifying on old pods
  until the rollout finishes. Finish rollouts promptly; that window
  is inherent to N/N−1.
- **Dev-push makes downgrades destructive** (Payload/drizzle prompts
  to delete the newer columns; accepting loses data, declining exits
  silently). Never roll back through a dev-push boot. Migrations
  mode boots old code read/write against the new schema safely
  (that is what the N−1 test proves).
- Schema changes follow expand → backfill → contract across two
  releases; a column that a previous minor cannot write against
  (NOT NULL without default, narrowed type) must never ship.

## Changing or removing roles

Roles are stored on user docs as plain slugs and validated for
**format** at the boundary, but grant only what the configured
`authLink({ roles })` allows (B11). When you remove or rename a
role, stored rows keep the old value until rewritten — so:

1. **Drain first.** Reassign every user holding the role to its
   replacement (admin panel or `payload.updateOne`) while the role
   is still configured.
2. **Then remove it** from `authLink({ roles })`.
3. **Boot and read the audit.** The first boot logs one aggregate
   warning — `N user doc(s) carry roles outside the configured set:
'editor' (2)` — if anything was missed. Sessions already stopped
   granting the removed role at that boot (reads filter it), and a
   user whose _only_ role was removed is denied a record entirely
   (never silently upgraded to the default role — same policy as
   corrupt roles).
4. Re-add the role to the config (temporarily) to drain properly if
   step 3 shows stragglers; clean rows keep the warning away on the
   next boot.

Renaming = add the new role, drain, remove the old one. The audit
runs on every boot (`onInit`) and costs one indexed query.

## Running production on migrations, not push

Dev-push (`push: true`) is for development: it makes destructive
choices interactively and makes downgrades lossy (above). Production
runs with `push: false` and explicit migrations:

1. Create the migration in your repo:

   ```sh
   payload.migrate:create   # or: bunx payload migrate:create
   ```

   Review the generated SQL before committing it. For the 0.1.1 →
   0.2.x move it must add `key` **nullable** (see above) and the
   optional governance columns — anything NOT NULL without a default
   is a bug in the migration, not in your database.

2. Run migrations as a deploy step, before new pods serve traffic:
   `payload.migrate` (or `bunx payload migrate`) in the release
   job. The expand→backfill→contract policy means migrations run
   cleanly while old-version pods still serve.
3. Keep the migration files in the repo — they are the record of
   how each release moves the database, and the artifact you attach
   to upgrade notes when you operate more than one environment.

The golden-DB tests (SQLite in `bun run check`; Postgres and Mongo
in the compat workflow) boot the previous release's seed under the
current code in both push and migrations modes, so a release that
would strand an upgraded database fails CI before it ships.

## 0.0.x → 0.1.0 (initial release)

First published line. No migration — but confirm before adopting:

- Packages are **ESM-only**. CJS `require()` of any entry (including
  `/cookies` subpaths) is unsupported; use ESM or dynamic import.
- The example's email-verification shortcuts
  (`requireEmailVerification: false`, immediate `emailVerified`
  stamps) are **local-dev-only**. Production must verify out-of-band.
- `payload.config.ts` collections for both providers are additive
  (`ba-*`, `aj-*`); the `users` extension adds `roles` +
  `identities` fields. No host migrations ship — your migration
  tooling owns schema changes (host-owned migrations only, per DNA).

## Session wire contract gains optional facts (PORT-4)

Additive only — no migration, and mixed versions keep working:

- **`SessionUser` and the plugin-level `Session` gain three optional
  fields**: `assurance` (`{ methods, mfa }`, how the session was
  proven), `actor` (`{ providerUserId }`, present only while an
  operator impersonates the user), and `organizationId` (the
  provider-native active tenant, when one is active). The session
  endpoint, the Payload auth strategy, the web verifier/`require*`
  helpers, and the React provider all carry them through.
- **Old payloads still parse.** A server that predates these fields
  simply omits them; clients see them as absent. Newer servers omit
  a field unless it is known — never `null`, never a fabricated
  default (a stray `null` for `actor`/`organizationId` is accepted
  and normalized to absent).
- **`'unknown'` assurance is data, not absence.** When the provider
  reported assurance but cannot tell the method or MFA state, the
  values serialize as `'unknown'`. Treat absent and `'unknown'`
  alike in policy: neither satisfies a requirement (fail closed) —
  but they stay distinguishable for diagnostics.
- **Malformed optional facts degrade, never nuke the user.** The
  client wire parser ignores unknown keys inside
  `assurance`/`actor` (forward compatibility with newer servers)
  and degrades a present-but-invalid optional
  fail-closed-for-policy (`assurance` to `'unknown'`,
  `actor`/`organizationId` to absent); core identity fields
  (`id`, `email`, `roles`) stay strict. An impersonation marker
  still cannot be laundered away server-side: authorization and
  audit use the plugin's own fail-closed extraction, where a
  present-but-malformed `actor` on `req.user` still denies and is
  audited as `actorKind: 'malformed-actor'`.

## Channel admission and impersonation completion (CAP-13a, CAP-8b)

- **`authLink({ admitChannels })` gates session channels.** It
  defaults to `['cookie']`: a live provider session presented on any
  other channel (`bearer`, `api-key`, `device`) is refused at
  verification with the typed `ChannelNotAdmittedError` (401),
  before any linking. Both shipped adapters report `cookie`, so
  existing behavior is unchanged. CSRF is unchanged too:
  state-changing endpoints still always require CSRF proof.
- **`Session.actor` and `SessionUser.actor` are now resolved.** The
  plugin looks the impersonating operator up by provider identity:
  a linked operator appears as
  `{ kind: 'payload-user', providerUserId, userId }` with the
  operator's Payload user id. An operator with no linked Payload
  user stays explicit: `{ kind: 'provider-only', providerUserId }`
  — fail-closed (the session still verifies and is audit-logged,
  but the provider id is never presented as a Payload id, and the
  unresolved state is logged as a warning). `parseSessionUser`
  accepts the legacy `{ providerUserId }` form and normalizes it to
  `provider-only`. `ProviderSession.actor` keeps the provider form.
- **Impersonated Payload operations are audited.** The plugin adds
  a `beforeOperation` hook to every collection and global that logs
  `impersonated operation` through `LoggerPort` with actor, target,
  operation, collection/global, and document id where named.
- **Impersonation is restricted by default (D5).** On the users
  collection the plugin now denies admin-panel access and writes to
  the roles field while an actor is present; reads are unaffected.
  For your own collections, `denyWhileImpersonating(ops?)` (plugin
  export) builds a matching `access` map — default denies `admin`,
  `create`, `update`, `delete`, and `unlock` while impersonating
  and allows reads — or gate on `isImpersonating(req)` inside your
  own access functions (fail-closed; `impersonationActorFromRequest`
  is for attribution only and returns `null` for a malformed actor
  that still denies).

## Hardening in the first release line (review backlog)

Behavior that tightened before first publish. Each change fails
closed, and none needs a data migration:

- **`authLink({ secret })` is deprecated and ignored.** Nothing in
  the plugin signs or encrypts: provider sessions are protected by
  the provider's own secret, and Payload auth by Payload's `secret`.
  The option stays optional so existing configs compile; delete it.
  `validateStartupConfig` (core) no longer accepts a `secret` key.
- **`safeRedirectPath` refuses sign-in and API destinations.** It
  falls back when the destination is the sign-in page (default
  `/sign-in`) or sits under `/api`. Pass
  `{ signInPath, apiPrefix }` to match custom mounts, or
  `{ signInPath: null }` where landing on sign-in is legitimate. It
  moved to core; `web`, `next` and `tanstack-start` re-export it
  unchanged.
- **`SignOutButton` narrows `redirectTo`** through
  `safeRedirectPath`. Off-origin and API destinations go to `/`.
- **`requireRoles` validates its role list first.** An invalid role
  (e.g. `'Admin'`) throws `InvalidRoleError`, and an empty list
  throws `InvalidConfigError`. Use `requireSessionUser` for "any
  signed-in user".
- **Wiring rejects illegal cookie attributes.** Provider session
  cookie names must be RFC 6265 tokens (checked at registration).
  Cookie `Domain`/`Path` values containing `;`, `,`, whitespace or
  control characters throw at serialization.
- **Auth.js `authorize` lowercases the email** exactly like
  registration, so `User@X.com` signs in. A corrupt stored
  `emailVerified` throws `AdapterMappingError`, and a gapped session
  chunk set is a failed read, never a joined token.
- **Clocks must be synchronized.** Session expiry has no skew
  leeway (see concepts).

## Future: WorkOS / Clerk adapters (post-v1)

Reserved registry ids, no packages yet. When they land they will be
new optional dependencies (`provider-workos`, `provider-clerk`)
following the same engine → port → collections shape — adopting one
is additive to the plugin options, never a rewrite.

---

<!-- docs/MISSION.md -->

# Mission

## Problem

`payload-auth/payload-auth` bolts Better Auth onto Payload CMS through
monkey-patches, stringly-typed schema maps, framework leaks, and `any`-heavy
plumbing. It fights Payload instead of extending it, so site builders inherit
its coupling, its silent fallbacks, and its upgrade risk.

## Mission

Build the enterprise-grade, strictly-typed, hexagonal replacement:
a Payload CMS v3 plugin that makes external identity providers
(Better Auth, Auth.js/NextAuth, WorkOS, Clerk) feel like first-class
Payload citizens — managed from Payload collections and the Payload admin —
while keeping every provider behind a swappable port.

## What "first-class Payload citizen" means

- Users live in a Payload collection. Roles, access control, hooks,
  validation, drafts, and versions behave exactly as in native Payload auth.
- Admins manage identities, linked accounts, and sessions from the
  Payload admin — no second dashboard, no out-of-band user store.
- The plugin follows Payload's plugin contract (`definePlugin`, strategies,
  endpoints, hooks, admin components, host-owned migrations) and never
  reaches around it.

## What "hexagonal" means here

- `core` owns the domain and the port interfaces; it imports no framework.
- Every external touchpoint — Payload storage, each identity provider,
  cookies/session transport, logging, tracing, transactions — is an adapter
  behind a port, registered explicitly at a composition root.
- Adding a provider means writing one adapter package, not touching the core.

## Provider roadmap

Initial build: Better Auth first, then Auth.js/NextAuth — the two
providers fully validatable with unit + e2e locally (self-hosted,
no SaaS dependency). Auth.js shipped after its research spike
(Phase 4): both adapters, integration tests, and e2e are green.

Deferred post-v1: WorkOS and Clerk. Both are SaaS-backed and cannot
be fully validated locally; their ports stay reserved in the design
(`IdentityProviderPort` + registry keyed by id) but no adapter
packages ship in the initial build.

No provider ships without its adapter, its integration tests, and its e2e
coverage.

## Non-goals

- No fork of, or compatibility layer for, `payload-auth` internals.
- No second user store, shadow session table, or out-of-band auth cookie.
- No framework code in `core`; no Payload imports in UI packages;
  no React in the plugin outside `admin/`.
- No `any` at module boundaries; no silent fallbacks; no `console.*`.

## Quality bar

Strict TypeScript, `neverthrow`-style `Result` errors at boundaries,
Zod-validated inputs, lint-enforced package boundaries, and mandatory e2e:
every auth flow (sign-in, callback, webhook sync, logout, session revoke)
is proven against a real Payload app in Playwright before release.

---

<!-- docs/DNA.md -->

# DNA — engineering constitution

How this repo is built. Every decision below traces to the research
synthesis (D1–D18) or to `payload-onpage` precedent. Violating these
rules requires updating this file first.

## 1. Architecture: ports and adapters

- `core` owns the domain and all port interfaces (`core/src/ports.ts`).
  It imports nothing framework-specific — no `payload`, no `next/*`,
  no React, no provider SDK.
- Adapters live at the leaves: one package per surface.
- Wiring happens only at an explicit composition root
  (factory functions like `nextSession()`, `payloadRest()`).
  No DI container (awilix/tsyringe/inversify rejected: magic,
  weak inference, worse tree-shaking).
- Constructor injection everywhere: `RegisterUser(repo, ids, clock)`.
- Public API is the explicit export list in each `index.ts`.
  Exporting something new is a decision, not a side effect.

### Package map (mirrors payload-onpage)

- `@scope/core` — framework-free: ports, domain (roles, session
  types, errors), provider-neutral orchestration. Depends on nothing.
- `@scope/plugin` — Payload server: plugin fn, collections/globals
  extension, AuthStrategy, endpoints, hooks, access, `admin/`.
  Depends on core + payload.
- `@scope/react` — provider-agnostic UI (sign-in buttons, user menu,
  admin helpers). No Next, no Payload imports.
- `@scope/next` — Next.js adapter: route handlers, middleware/proxy,
  cookie/session helpers. Depends on core + react.
- `@scope/provider-<id>` — one package per identity provider.
  Initial build: `better-auth` first, `authjs` after its spike (both shipped, Phase 4).
  `workos` and `clerk` deferred post-v1 (SaaS-backed, not locally
  validatable); the registry reserves their ids.
- `examples/basic` — reference integration and e2e target (SQLite,
  self-seeding, like onpage's `:3100` example).

### v1 ports

- `UserRepository` — users via Payload Local API (never raw DB).
- `SessionPort` — verify/create/revoke sessions; strategies delegate here.
- `IdentityProviderPort` — per-IdP authorize/callback/webhook/profile
  normalize; instances registered in an adapter registry keyed by id.
- `CookiePort` — read/write/clear; implemented by the framework adapter.
- `TransactionPort`, `LoggerPort`, `TracerPort` — storage transactions,
  structured logs, spans. `ClockPort` + `IdPort` for determinism.

### Dependency rules (lint-enforced via `no-restricted-imports`)

- core imports no framework. react imports no Next/Payload.
  plugin imports no React outside `admin/`.
- Sources import siblings with `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Cross-package imports use workspace package names, never deep paths
  outside declared subpath exports.

## 2. Payload contract

- Plugin shape: `definePlugin<TOptions>({ slug, order, plugin })`;
  `(options) => (incomingConfig) => Config`. Copy config, spread-append
  collections/globals, merge hook objects (never overwrite), chain
  `onInit`, return config. Lower `order` first; cross-plugin via `plugins` map.
- Auth strategy: `{ name, authenticate({ headers, payload, req, ... }) }`
  returning `{ user: { ...doc, collection } } | null`. Read-only session
  checks use refresh-disabled reads (no login loops).
- `auth.strategies[]` plus explicit cookies/token/api-key options.
- Custom `endpoints[]` are unauthenticated by default: check `req.user`,
  method lowercase, `handler(req: PayloadRequest) => Response`.
  Every state-changing endpoint gets a CSRF guard + access check —
  authorization goes through one `access.ts` using Payload's access ops.
- Preserve existing hooks when extending (append, don't replace);
  inject admin/meta fields as a group. Root/collection/global/field
  hooks are awaited in series; `afterError` may transform.
- Admin UI is React Server Components by default; `'use client'` only
  where needed, registered as `{ path#Export, clientProps/serverProps }`.
- Migrations are host-owned (`up`/`down`, `migrate:create/status/down`).
  The plugin ships no migration mechanism.

## 3. Coupling guardrails (the payload-auth anti-patterns, banned)

- No double-pass init: resolve schemas once, before hooks/endpoints/
  `useAsTitle` attach — never build-collections → sync → rebuild.
- No monkey-patch contract: no `Object.defineProperty(payload, …)`,
  no string flags on `config.custom`, no per-invocation client
  re-entry from strategies/hooks/endpoints. Typed injected client
  from the composition root instead.
- No framework leak: no `next/headers` (or any framework import)
  inside Payload hooks or core. Cookie/transport work lives in the
  framework adapter (`toNextJsHandler`, `nextCookies()`).
- No stringly schema map: typed slug/field maps with explicit errors.
  No silent fallbacks, no "warns but uses wrong slug", no runtime
  patching of provider internals.
- No hand-rolled sessions: no admin-session hacks, manual `Set-Cookie`
  concat, or fabricated endpoint contexts. Sessions go through
  `SessionPort` + `CookiePort`.

## 4. Type safety

- `strict` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `noUnused*`.
  Guard indexes; never assert (`!`). Options filled from other
  optionals are typed `?: T | undefined`.
- Zero-`any` boundary: no `: any`, no `as` casts at module edges,
  no whole-instance erasure (`as unknown as …`). Sanitize by deep-copy,
  never shallow-spread-then-deep-write the caller's options.
- Generics survive: provider/plugin options preserve their type
  parameters end to end (no hardcoded generated-types artifact that
  silently drops endpoints when plugins change).
- One canonical `Role` type with a smart constructor at the boundary.
  No `array | string | comma-string` branching at every call site;
  normalize once, use everywhere.
- Make the compiler check it: discriminated unions + `assertNever`,
  branded keys for document refs, readiness guards before reading
  loaded state, typed message catalogs for UI strings.

## 5. Errors and validation

- Expected failures return `neverthrow` `Result<T, E>` /
  `ResultAsync` (`ok`/`err`, `fromThrowable`, `combine`,
  `fromPromise`/`fromSafePromise`). Throw only for the truly unexpected.
- Domain errors vs application errors stay distinct
  (`InvalidEmailError` vs `UserExistsError`); the web adapter maps
  them to status codes. Never swallow (`null`/`[]`/`0` on failure),
  never drop nulls, never leave endpoints unauthenticated by accident.
- Validate at every untyped boundary with Zod
  (`safeParse`/`safeParseAsync`, `z.infer`, `.strict()`).
  Zod over TypeBox: distinct `z.input`/`z.output` and superior error
  reporting matter more here than schema-reuse speed, and validation
  sits off the session hot path.
- Startup validation fails fast: baseURL/secret present, default role
  inside roles, adapter-boundary schemas valid.

## 6. Observability

- Domain depends on `LoggerPort` + `TracerPort` only. Adapters use
  pino (child loggers per module, `serializers.err`, never untrusted
  keys) and OpenTelemetry spans, injected — never imported.
- No `console.*` anywhere. Forward into Payload's pino instance and
  the provider logger where supported.
- No hardcoded query depth: depth is configurable per call site.
- Transactions go through `TransactionPort` — no no-op stubs.

## 7. Testing constitution (e2e is mandatory)

- Unit tests live next to code in `src/__tests__/`.
- Integration tests run real Payload on in-memory SQLite through
  `handleEndpoints` (onpage precedent), or the Local API over a
  memory DB with fixtures (`config`, `resetBetweenTests`).
- Behavior change → test. Security change → an integration test
  that fails without the fix.
- Playwright e2e runs against `examples/basic` with a fresh DB:
  sign-in, OAuth callback, webhook user-sync, logout, session
  revoke from the admin, role-gated access. Chromium, retries on CI,
  traces retained on failure, axe for admin UI regressions.
- DB strategy: SQLite in-memory for local/unit, `mongodb-memory-server`
  replica set for integration default, containerized Postgres for
  parity in CI.
- `bun run check` gates everything: format, lint, typecheck,
  coverage thresholds, build, size budgets. No merge on red.

## 8. Repo conventions

- Bun monorepo: `packages/*` + `examples/*` workspaces, `tsc -b` build,
  `publint` + `are-the-types-wrong` on publishable packages.
- Prettier: single quotes, no semicolons, width 100.
  typescript-eslint type-checked, react-hooks, jsx-a11y.
- Changesets required for user-facing changes; provenance-enabled
  publishes; `SECURITY.md` for private reports.
- Public API → TSDoc plus `docs/` guides. Docs follow the onpage
  system as they grow: tour, getting-started, concepts, guides,
  compatibility, troubleshooting, upgrading — plus `llms.txt` and
  `AGENTS.md` for agent consumers.
- Never commit secrets, never log credentials, never ship a release
  with debug output (release hygiene is a checklist item, not a hope).

## 9. Security invariants

- Never link a provider identity to an existing user, or reuse an
  existing email for a provider login, unless the provider verified the
  email (`emailVerified`). Unverified profiles must not take over
  existing accounts; creation of a standalone user is the provider's
  verification lifecycle to complete.
- State-changing endpoints require CSRF proof: matching `Origin` or a
  custom header a cross-site page cannot set. Redirect targets are
  validated same-origin against `baseUrl` — never an open redirect.

---

<!-- docs/PLAN.md -->

## Goal

Replace `payload-auth/payload-auth` with a greenfield Payload CMS v3
plugin: hexagonal ports/adapters, strict typesafe, enterprise grade,
where Better Auth (first) and Auth.js/NextAuth integrate as swappable
adapters while users stay first-class Payload documents managed from
the Payload admin. WorkOS and Clerk are deferred post-v1 (SaaS-backed,
not fully validatable locally). Research is done (9-agent workflow,
synthesis `complete:true`); this plan turns decisions D1–D18 plus
payload-onpage precedent into shippable phases.

## Success Criteria

- A site builder installs packages, adds one plugin call, and signs
  in via Better Auth with users/roles/sessions in Payload collections.
- Each provider is an isolated adapter package; core has zero
  framework imports (lint-proven).
- Zero `any` at boundaries; generic-preserving option types;
  canonical `Role` type; `Result`-based errors; Zod boundaries.
- Full e2e: sign-in, callback, webhook sync, logout, admin session
  revoke — green in CI before any release.
- Docs a builder can follow: tour, getting-started, guides, plus
  `llms.txt`/`AGENTS.md` for agent consumers.

## Approach

Clone the proven payload-onpage monorepo shape (core ports,
framework adapters, example app as e2e target, `check` pipeline),
fill it with the auth domain from the synthesis, and ship the two
locally-validatable providers behind `IdentityProviderPort`.
Better Auth first (researched); Auth.js gated on a short research
spike since only Better Auth bodies were inspected. WorkOS and Clerk
stay out of the initial build; the registry reserves their ids.
Re-verify every delegated-research claim against installed `payload`
types and official docs at implementation start; unresolved items
below stay open until then.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Scaffold and tooling

- Bun monorepo: `packages/{core,plugin,react,next}`,
  `packages/provider-better-auth`, `examples/basic`, `e2e/`.
- TS `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` +
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` + `verbatimModuleSyntax` + `noUnused*`;
  eslint `no-restricted-imports` boundaries; Prettier; `tsc -b`.
- `check` script: format, lint, typecheck, coverage gates, build,
  size budgets. Changesets, `publint`, `are-the-types-wrong`.
- `examples/basic`: SQLite, self-seeding, reference integration.
- `docs/` skeleton, `AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Phase 1 — Core domain and ports

- `ports.ts`: `UserRepository`, `SessionPort`,
  `IdentityProviderPort` + registry, `CookiePort`, `TransactionPort`,
  `LoggerPort`, `TracerPort`, `ClockPort`, `IdPort`.
- Canonical `Role` + smart constructor; typed slug/field map;
  `Result<T,E>` error taxonomy; Zod boundary schemas; startup
  validation (baseURL/secret, default-role-in-roles).
- Explicit composition-root factories. No DI container.
- Unit tests next to code; public API = explicit `index.ts` lists.

### Phase 2 — Payload plugin (first-class citizenship)

- `definePlugin` shape: copy config, append collections/globals,
  merge hooks, chain `onInit`.
- Users collection extension (identities, roles, sessions views),
  custom `AuthStrategy` delegating to `SessionPort`, unauthenticated-
  by-default endpoints with CSRF guard + `access.ts`, hook appends,
  RSC admin components (`path#Export`).
- Correctness starters: `pagination:false` on logout finds,
  forward+reverse joins, refresh-disabled session reads,
  configurable query depth. Host-owned migrations only.

### Phase 3 — Better Auth + Next.js adapters

- `provider-better-auth`: `betterAuth({ database: payloadAdapter,
plugins })`, session/cookie delegation, no `next/headers` outside
  the Next adapter, no hand-rolled cookies.
- `@scope/next`: route handlers (`/api/auth/[...all]`), proxy/
  middleware, `nextCookies()` (Edge optimistic + Node full
  validation), `<Provider />`, `useNextRefresh`-style renderer.
- `@scope/react`: sign-in buttons, user menu, admin helpers.
- Integration tests on SQLite-in-memory via `handleEndpoints`;
  security tests that fail without each guard.

### Phase 4 — Auth.js spike, then adapter ✅ DONE

- Spike (`spike.test.ts`, 6/6): Credentials is JWT-only and ignores
  the adapter; credentials + `database` strategy is rejected at
  config time (`UnsupportedStrategy`); the jwt callback re-runs
  without `user` on reads (guard claims); the port reads via Auth's
  own session action (`skipCSRFCheck`, no hand JWT decode).
- `packages/provider-authjs` behind `IdentityProviderPort` +
  registry: engine (fail-fasts, `/api/authjs` basePath,
  claims-callback chaining), Payload database adapter (users,
  accounts, sessions, verification tokens, authenticators), scrypt
  credentials service with builder-stamped verification, port with
  chunk-joining session-id extraction, edge-safe `/cookies` subpath.
- Example coexistence: Auth.js mounted alongside Better Auth
  (`lib/authjs.ts`, `/api/authjs/[...authjs]`, builder-owned
  `/api/authjs-signup`, `/sign-in-authjs` page, concatenated
  middleware cookie names). E2E finding: @auth/core's credentials
  callback always 302s (`json=true` is a v4 convention it ignores) —
  the form follows the redirect and reads success/failure from the
  final URL (`?error=…` on reject).
- Validation: 67 provider tests (unit + SQLite adapter lifecycle +
  error mapping), `bun run check` green, 3 Auth.js e2e specs green.
- WorkOS and Clerk: no spike, no adapter in the initial build
  (deferred post-v1; registry ids reserved).

### Phase 5 — E2E, CI, release hygiene ✅ DONE

- Playwright against `examples/basic` + fresh DB: sign-in,
  callback, webhook sync, logout, admin revoke, role-gated access,
  axe on admin UI. Chromium, CI retries, traces on failure.
  ✅ Local e2e green: 10/10 (Better Auth sign-up/in/out + wrong
  password + role gate + users-admin + smoke + 3 Auth.js specs).
  Remaining: axe pass on admin UI, CI retries/traces already
  configured in `playwright.config.ts`.
- CI matrix: SQLite local, `mongodb-memory-server` replset,
  containerized Postgres parity. Coverage gates enforced.
  ✅ `ci.yml` (check + e2e + release-check jobs, trace artifacts).
  ✅ Postgres: `e2e:postgres` + `dev:e2e-pg`, per-run database,
  13/13 in 11 of 13 runs (two `users-admin` admin-list wait failures;
  structural causes ruled out with DB evidence — no seed dupes,
  no pagination, fresh DB per run — leaving transient slowness;
  spec wait split for diagnosis, CI `retries: 2` covers the
  class). No compose file — GH `services:` in CI, `docker run`
  locally.
  ✅ Mongo: `e2e:mongo` via `e2e/run-mongo.mjs` (per-run
  wiredTiger replset, `transactionOptions: false` in the example's
  mongo branch — three Payload instances lock-fight on one node,
  and our adapters never use multi-doc transactions), 13/13 x3.
  ✅ `ci.yml`: `e2e` (sqlite) + `e2e-postgres` (service) +
  `e2e-mongo` (memory replset) + `check` + `release:check`.
  Note: run parity suites separately, not chained — three
  back-to-back suites saturate one box (mongo leg timed out
  in-chain, 13/13 in 17s solo; CI isolates per job).
- Release checklist: changesets, provenance, no debug output,
  no logged credentials (anti-#154). ✅ Wired: `.changeset/`
  config, `release`/`version-packages` scripts, `release.yml`
  (trusted publishing, provenance), `CONTRIBUTING.md` release
  section. `bun run release:check` (`publint` + `attw --profile
esm-only`) green on all 6 packages as a pre-publish gate
  (kept out of `check` for speed; runs in CI).

### Phase 6 — Builder docs ✅ DONE

- ✅ Tour, getting-started (four-edit drop-in: install, engine,
  config, routes+UI), concepts, Better Auth + Auth.js guides,
  compatibility, troubleshooting, upgrading — all in `docs/`.
- ✅ `docs:api` (typedoc, 0 errors), `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt`
  (generated by `bun run docs:llms`, drift-proof), media from the
  example app (`bun run docs:media`, 5 screenshots in
  `docs/media/`). Every public API has TSDoc (audit clean).
- ✅ Fresh-eyes validation: independent agent audit of every guide
  snippet against source — 7 factual wrongs found and fixed
  (route import depth, BA model/field constraints, error names,
  measured JWT size, dep classification), plus nits.

## Validation Plan

- Phase 0: `bun run check` green on empty packages; example boots
  and seeds (`bun run dev:example`).
- Phase 1: `vitest run --coverage` passes gates; eslint proves
  core imports no framework; type tests prove generics survive.
- Phase 2: integration suite green on SQLite memory;
  `pagination:false`/join/refresh-disabled behaviors covered;
  admin renders users + identities + sessions.
- Phase 3: Better Auth sign-in/callback/logout pass in
  integration; route-handler + middleware tests green.
- Phase 4: Auth.js integration suite green before merge. ✅
  (67 tests + 3 e2e specs green, `check` green.)
- Phase 5: `bun run e2e` green locally and in CI across DBs;
  highest-risk gate — no release without it. ✅ Local: 16/16 on
  sqlite + postgres + mongo; CI runs all three plus check and
  release-check (first CI run happens on first push — no remote
  yet).
- Phase 6: fresh-clone walkthrough of getting-started by a
  second person (or agent) with zero prior context. ✅ Proxy:
  independent agent audit of all guides vs source; all findings
  fixed and re-verified against source. True fresh-clone still
  wants a human on first publish (no remote yet).

## Known issues, resolved post-Phase 6

- ✅ Auth.js factory-provider bypass: the engine now inspects
  factories the way Auth.js normalizes them (called with `{}`),
  so wrapped credentials fail fast; factories that throw on
  inspection surface `InvalidConfigError` at wiring time.
- ✅ Auth.js giant-claim chunks: `chunkSlots` on the engine input
  (default 3) sizes the session-cookie slots; the middleware names
  mirror it. Only tokens past the raised slots need Auth.js's own
  signout action.
- ✅ Better Auth custom fields + plugin models: `customFields` /
  `customModels` engine options generate matching Payload columns
  and extend the adapter allowlist; strict both directions
  (undeclared extras, declared-but-absent names, and undeclared
  plugin models all throw `UnsupportedSchemaError` at startup).
- ✅ Enterprise review hardening (multi-agent review + fixes):
  open-redirect guard (`safeRedirectPath`, both example forms, e2e);
  logout clears with live cookie attributes (`Secure`/`Domain` via
  `sessionCookieClearOptions`, prefix-derived fallback); server
  authorization helpers (`requireSessionUser`/`requireRoles`,
  example admin page enforced on Node, e2e proves the secret never
  ships to denied callers); credentials dummy-hash anti-oracle;
  `baseUrl`-anchored session reads (host fallback dev-only);
  unified error taxonomy (BA `AdapterOperationError` under
  `AuthLinkError`); Auth.js slug validation parity
  (`resolveSlugs`/`assertUniqueSlugs`, custom-model collision
  checks); shared core guards (`isRecord`/`toDate`,
  `runProviderOperation`, `denyAllAccess`). 331 unit + 17×6 e2e
  green (Next + TanStack × SQLite/Postgres/Mongo; see
  PLAN-TANSTACK.md).
  Proven by `custom-schema.test.ts` (additionalFields round-trip +
  organization/member/invitation CRUD on SQLite memory).
- ⏸️ Postgres `users-admin` intermittence (~2/13 runs): structural
  causes ruled out with container evidence; split-wait added for
  diagnosis; CI `retries: 2` covers. Revisit if it ever fails twice
  in a row or appears on sqlite/mongo.
- ⏸️ Next.js `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts` rename (Next 16
  deprecation warning, log noise only): staying on `middleware.ts`
  deliberately — `proxy.ts` needs Next 16+ and the peer range is
  `>=15`. Revisit when the floor rises.

## Risks / Open Questions

- ~~Only Better Auth integration bodies inspected; Auth.js needs
  its spike (Phase 4).~~ RESOLVED in Phase 4: spike green, adapter
  - port + engine shipped, session-verify sync proven by e2e.
    (No webhooks in either provider path — sync is read-time via the
    port, not webhook-to-users.) WorkOS/Clerk spikes explicitly out
    of scope.
- Access `Where` shape, full hook arg shapes, `templates/plugin`
  3.x source not inspected — verify against installed types in
  Phase 0/2, not from memory.
- No official Payload testing docs (404) and no published
  `@payloadcms/test` — harness follows onpage precedent
  (SQLite memory + `handleEndpoints` + Playwright on example).
- ~~Postgres parity mechanism (compose vs replset vs testcontainers)
  undecided — spike in Phase 5, default to compose.~~ RESOLVED:
  no compose file — GH `services: postgres:16` in CI, `docker run`
  locally, per-run database names; mongo via in-process
  `mongodb-memory-server` replset (wiredTiger, no transactions).
- payload-auth issue bodies beyond titles and audit-rec landing
  status unconfirmed — re-verify anti-patterns against its `main`
  at Phase 1 start so guardrails track reality.

## Sources

<!-- docs/PLAN-TANSTACK.md -->

# TanStack Start support plan

## Goal

Make TanStack Start a first-class citizen alongside Next.js: a sibling
framework adapter (`@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start`) built on the
same hexagonal ports, so site builders get identical auth behavior on
either framework with zero provider changes. Day-one target is
Payload v4 (TanStack support ships in `v4.0.0-beta.0`, not v3).

## Success Criteria

- A builder wires Better Auth or Auth.js into a TanStack Start app
  with the same calls as Next: engine, collections, provider
  registration, route mounting, session verification, role
  enforcement.
- The Next and TanStack adapters share one implementation of every
  framework-free behavior (no forked copies).
- A TanStack example app runs both providers with 16/16 e2e green,
  in CI, on SQLite at minimum.
- `bun run check` and `bun run release:check` cover the new
  package; guides document the Start path.

## Approach

Mirror Payload's own adapter pattern: thin framework package over
shared UI. Payload renders one `@payloadcms/ui` behind
`@payloadcms/next` and `@payloadcms/tanstack-start`; we render one
`@payload-auth-link/react` behind `@payload-auth-link/next` and the
new `@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start`.

Four of the seven Next modules are already framework-free
(`handlers`, `verify`, `authz`, `redirect` — pure
Request/Response/Headers/fetch). They move to a new shared
`@payload-auth-link/web` package; `next` re-exports them so existing
imports keep working. Only `middleware`, `client`, and
`server-provider` stay Next-only (`next/server`, `next/navigation`,
`next/headers`). The Start package then holds only Start imports,
per DNA §3 (no framework leak outside the adapter).

Payload constraint: `@payloadcms/tanstack-start` exists only on the
v4 line (beta, no stable). Our plugin peers `payload ^3.0.0` and the
Next example runs 3.90.2, so Phase 0 is a go/no-go compat spike
before any adapter code.

## Capability mapping

| Capability            | Next today                       | Start target                       |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Mount provider routes | `createRouteHandlers` → GET/POST | Same handlers in `server.handlers` |
| Catch-all API shape   | `[...all]/route.ts`              | `api/auth/$.ts` splat route        |
| Optimistic bounce     | `createAuthMiddleware`           | `createMiddleware().server()`      |
| Server session read   | `createSessionVerifier`          | Shared; headers via `getRequest()` |
| Role enforcement      | `requireRoles`                   | Shared; called from `beforeLoad`   |
| Hydration             | `AuthLinkServerProvider`         | Root `loader` + `initialUser`      |
| Post-auth refresh     | `router.refresh()`               | `router.invalidate()`              |
| Redirect safety       | `safeRedirectPath`               | Shared unchanged                   |
| BA framework plugin   | `nextCookies()`                  | `tanstackStartCookies()`           |

## Steps

### Phase 0 — v4-compat spike ✅ DONE — GO

- Scaffolded `examples/tanstack-start` on `payload@4.0.0-beta.0` +
  `@payloadcms/tanstack-start@4.0.0-beta.0` (file routes per PR
  #16139: `__root.tsx` shell, `_payload` layout, `api.$.ts`).
- Plugin loads under v4 beta with **zero changes**: collections
  register, strategy + endpoints serve, onInit seeds.
- Better Auth signup → session read (JIT user, `roles: [user]`) →
  logout (both providers' cookies expired) verified over HTTP;
  Auth.js mount verified (`/api/authjs/csrf` 200); admin renders.

Findings (all recorded from the spike session):

- **GO.** No plugin rewrite needed; both engines round-trip.
- v4 flips the Local API access default: builder code (seeds,
  scripts) must pass `overrideAccess: true`. Every shipped
  plugin/provider Local API call already does (audited).
- `withPayload` requires the caller to apply `rsc(pluginOptions.rsc)`
  (else SSR 500s); `@vitejs/plugin-rsc` +
  `react-server-dom-webpack` are required dev deps.
- `devServerExternalPackages: ['ajv']` required — ajv's CJS breaks
  under the RSC rewrite (frozen namespace hits `uri.code = ...`).
- Server route handlers receive `{ request }` context, not a bare
  `Request` — shapes the Phase 2 `createServerRouteHandlers` API.
- Spike ran under node; `bun run dev` for this example is untested
  (verify in Phase 3, fall back to node for the e2e webServer).
- `importMap.js` stub suffices for page load; run the real
  `payload generate:importmap` in Phase 3 for admin components.
- Pinned: payload 4.0.0-beta.0, Start 1.168.61, Router 1.170.41,
  vite 8.3.4, react 19.2.6.

### Phase 1 — Extract `@payload-auth-link/web` ✅ DONE

- Moved `handlers`, `verify`, `authz`, `redirect` + tests verbatim
  to the new package; no behavior change.
- `next` re-exports the moved API (back-compat); `next` depends on
  `web`; build refs, typedoc extended (vitest + release-check
  auto-discover).
- Validation: `bun run check` green, 315 unit green,
  `release:check` passes for all 7 packages, Next e2e 16/16 —
  zero regression proven.

### Phase 2 — `@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start` ✅ DONE

- `createServerRouteHandlers(handle)` → `{ GET, POST }` for
  `server.handlers` (uniform error envelope, same as Next).
- `createAuthRequestMiddleware()` — optimistic cookie-presence
  bounce to sign-in via `createMiddleware().server()` (parity
  default; document live-verify as optional hardening).
- Session server functions: `getSessionUser()` via `createServerFn`
  - `getRequest()` headers into the shared verifier
    (`baseUrl`-anchored, CSRF middleware per Start docs).
- `createSessionLoader()` for root-route hydration into
  `AuthLinkProvider initialUser`; `useAuthLinkRefreshStart()`
  (refresh + `router.invalidate()`).
- `beforeLoad` guard recipe using shared `requireRoles` (no new
  authz code).
- Better Auth engine gains a `tanstackStartCookies` plugin option
  mirroring `nextCookies` (verified exported by the installed
  better-auth 1.7.7 `better-auth/tanstack-start` subpath; Auth.js
  needs nothing — `handleRequest` is already Request/Response).
- Unit tests mirror the Next suite (middleware bounce matrix,
  handler envelope, loader hydration, refresh).
- Package re-exports the shared `web` API (same one-import DX as
  `next`).
- Validation: `bun run check` green, 331 unit green (16 new
  - BA engine), `release:check` passes all 8 packages.

### Phase 3 — `examples/tanstack-start` + e2e ✅ DONE

- Example on Payload v4 beta: both providers, sign-in forms,
  account page, server-guarded admin page, Payload admin.
- The 16-spec e2e suite runs unchanged against it (one suite, two
  frameworks — shared `admin-denied` marker, hydration-tolerant
  `gotoOwn`/`toggleToSignUp`, v3/v4 `listTable`/`listCell`
  locators); CI jobs `e2e-tanstack`, `e2e-tanstack-postgres`,
  `e2e-tanstack-mongo`.
- Postgres/Mongo matrix extension done in-phase: 16/16 on all six
  suites (Next + Start × SQLite/Postgres/Mongo).

Findings (all recorded from the Phase 3 session):

- SSR streams before hydration: suite clicks that land in the
  window are silently lost. Both examples render a
  `HydratedMarker` (`html[data-hydrated]`) and the suite waits
  for it (`gotoOwn`).
- `/_serverFn/` must stay public in Start request middleware —
  bouncing RPC corrupts the server-function protocol (redirect
  followed with a JSON Accept → Start 406 → admin detail crash
  on SPA navigation).
- TanStack `redirect()` / `notFound()` must be **thrown** in
  `requireRoles` handlers, not returned.
- v4 admin list renders `grid`/`gridcell` (same `<table>` markup,
  so tbody a11y scoping holds); v4 login adds a show-password
  toggle; v4 ID cells carry an upstream `.id-label` contrast
  failure (triaged exclusion, no-op on v3).
- `bun run dev` verified for the example; no node fallback needed.
- ⏸️ One transient (1/6 runs): post-login SSR to
  `/admin/collections/users` 307-bounced with a valid
  `payload-token` while a later `/me` succeeded — same class as
  the known parallel-worker admin intermittence; CI `retries: 2`
  covers. Revisit if it ever fails twice in a row.

### Phase 4 — Docs + release ✅ DONE

- `docs/guide-tanstack-start.md`, concepts/tour/compatibility
  updates, getting-started + guide-better-auth pointers, PLAN
  counts, llms regen, changesets (minor).
- `release:check` green for all 8 packages; publish together.

## Validation Plan

- Phase 0: scratch app boots, plugin loads, one provider
  round-trip each (manual + recorded findings doc).
- Phase 1: `bun run check`, `bunx vitest run` (315 green),
  `bun run e2e` (16/16, proves zero Next regression).
- Phase 2: new package unit suite green; `bun run release:check`
  covers it.
- Phase 3: TanStack e2e 16/16 on SQLite locally + CI job green
  (plus Postgres/Mongo matrix, done in-phase).
- Highest-risk gate: Phase 0 v4-compat outcome — everything downstream
  depends on the plugin loading under the v4 beta.

## Risks / Open Questions

- **v4 beta churn.** The adapter pins `4.0.0-beta.x`; beta API drift
  may force re-spikes. Mitigation: narrow peer range, Phase 0 records
  exact versions, CI pins lockfile.
- **Should the Next example migrate to v4?** No — stays on v3 until
  v4 stable. Separate work, tracked as a non-goal here.
- **Start middleware runs server-side** (unlike Edge), so full live
  verification is possible there; v1 ships optimistic parity and
  documents the upgrade.
- No Solid/Vue Start flavors in scope.

## Non-goals

- Payload v4 migration of the Next example or existing packages
  beyond what Phase 0 requires.
- TanStack Solid / Vue variants.
- Depending on a future payloadcms.com beta TanStack wiring doc —
  none was found; the PR and demo repo are the wiring reference.

## Sources

- https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/16139
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/payloadcms/payload-tanstack-demo/HEAD/README.md
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@payloadcms/tanstack-start
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@payloadcms/next/latest
- https://api.github.com/repos/payloadcms/payload/releases?per_page=5
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/server-functions
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/server-routes
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/middleware
- https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading
